updates.модальность: Larval thermal-gradient behavior (thermotaxis) and high-temperature probe-evoked curling; separate dTRPA1 immunostaining localizes protein in brain neurons and corpus cardiacum.
updates.задача: Test the role of dTRPA1 in Drosophila larval thermotaxis and distinguish thermal-gradient behavior from high-temperature probe-evoked nociceptive behavior.
updates.метод: The study uses dsRNA knockdown of dTrpA1 and other TRP genes, then tests larval thermal preference on a temperature gradient. Separate behavioral tests expose crawling third-instar larvae to a 55-57 degrees C probe and record curling/withdrawal; dTrpA1-Gal4-driven TeTxLC or Hid tests dTRPA1-expressing-cell contributions. The article separately uses dTRPA1 immunostaining; it does not report stimulus-evoked neural activity recording.
updates.датасет: Study-specific Drosophila larval behavioral assays and genetic manipulations reported in Figures 1-4; no external benchmark dataset is identified in the article.
updates.производительность: Not applicable: the article reports biological behavioral outcomes, not predictive-model performance. Figure 3C reports time from hot-probe contact to curling, and Figure 4H reports probe-response comparators.
updates.ограничения: Drosophila larval thermal-gradient and hot-probe behaviors only. The matrix-relevant negative result is specific to dTrpA1 RNAi larvae in the approximately 55 degrees C probe assay (Figures 3B-C); it does not establish that dTRPA1 is irrelevant to all nociception. Thermotaxis and high-temperature probe response are distinct behavioral endpoints. No subjective pain or human clinical outcome is measured; immunostaining is not stimulus-evoked neural activity recording.
